quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should be near the front because:

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them easily.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them closely.

questions.question: The best lane position:

options.text: Is always the right side of the lane.
Is always the center of the lane.
Is always the left side of the lane.
Depends on the road, weather, and traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the road, weather, and traffic.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on how conditions change.

questions.question: Which protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from the wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: At a stopped intersection, use your mirrors to:

options.text: See if parked cars are entering traffic.
Watch for cars behind you that may not be slowing down.
See if someone plans to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for cars behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: At a stopped intersection, check your mirrors for cars approaching from behind. The drivers may not see you in time.

questions.question: When a group passes another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider starts.
Have several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider fully pass before the next rider starts.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish their pass and return to formation before the next rider begins.

questions.question: If someone tailgates you, you should:

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up makes it more dangerous. Never ride on the shoulder—drivers don't expect you there.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, maintain a following distance of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance in poor conditions.

questions.question: Which provides the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Gradually apply the brake on the good tire. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night compared to during the day, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Allow more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: To stay safe when riding at night, ride slower and stay farther away from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space should:

options.text: Not be necessary in most situations.
Be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change based on riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space between vehicles if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance from other vehicles if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, they should:

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean with you when you turn. They should sit as far forward as comfortable without crowding you. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers can see you easily.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, so they are hard to see. Ride defensively and assume that other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: Which of the following is usually a rectangular sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a friend from driving while drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Ask other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drunk driving, offer them a ride home, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, find any reason to keep them from leaving, and get friends to help pressure them not to drive.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. For motorcyclists, this area is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this area has enough grip for safe riding. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can often ride around it while staying in the center lane.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever up to go to a higher gear. Push it down to go to a lower gear.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: You operate the rear brake of a motorcycle with your right foot.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group of motorcycles should ride in:
questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best most of the time. However, switch to single-file when turning, riding through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Other drivers should:

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle anytime.
Share a lane with a motorcycle during heavy traffic.
Share a lane with a motorcycle when entering a highway.
Never share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never share a lane with a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Both motorcycles and cars need a full lane width to operate safely. Lane sharing is not allowed.

questions.question: What best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide this protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar downhill:

options.text: Stopping is easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer than without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which means you need more braking force to stop. Stopping takes longer going downhill and with extra weight.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting.

questions.question: Successful motorcyclists know they are safest when:

options.text: They are faster than other vehicles.
They are on the side of the road.
They are on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other drivers can see them.
questions.explanation: Successful motorcyclists stay safe by being seen clearly by other drivers. Use your headlight, brake light, turn signals, and proper lane position to increase visibility.
